import io, sys

from astropy.table import QTable

failures = []
tbl = QTable({"wave": [350, 950] * u.nm, "response": [0.7, 1.2] * u.count})

out = io.StringIO()
tbl.write(out, format="ascii.rst")
expected_default = (
    "===== ========\n"

    "===== ========\n"

out = io.StringIO()
tbl.write(out, format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit"])
expected = (
    "===== ========\n"
    " wave response\n"
    "   nm       ct\n"
    "===== ========\n"
    "350.0      0.7\n"
    "950.0      1.2\n"
    "===== ========\n"
)
if out.getvalue() != expected:
    failures.append(f"header_rows=['name','unit'] mismatch:\n{out.getvalue()!r}")

# 3) fixed_width output must be unchanged
out = io.StringIO()
tbl.write(out, format="ascii.fixed_width", header_rows=["name", "unit"])
expected_fw = (
    "|  wave | response |\n"
    "|    nm |       ct |\n"
    "| 350.0 |      0.7 |\n"
    "| 950.0 |      1.2 |\n"
)
if out.getvalue() != expected_fw:
    failures.append(f"fixed_width mismatch:\n{out.getvalue()!r}")

# 4) Round-trip read/write with name+unit+dtype rows (upstream PR test scenario)

    "  950.0      2.0    2",
    "======= ======== ====",
]

    failures.append(f"response unit: {tbl2['response'].unit!r}")
if tbl2["wave"].dtype != np.float64:
    failures.append(f"wave dtype: {tbl2['wave'].dtype!r}")
if tbl2["response"].dtype != np.float32:
    failures.append(f"response dtype: {tbl2['response'].dtype!r}")
if tbl2["ints"].dtype != np.int8:

if failures:

args.summary: Supported `header_rows` in the RestructuredText (ascii.rst) writer. Diagnosis: `astropy/io/ascii/rst.py`'s `RST.__init__(self)` accepted no kwargs, so the `header_rows` kwarg (which `ui.write`/`core._get_writer` pass straight through to the writer class, and which the `FixedWidth` machinery in `fixedwidth.py` already fully implements — `FixedWidth.__init__` stores `header.header_rows`/`data.header_rows` and `FixedWidthData.write` emits one line per entry) raised `TypeError: RST.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'header_rows'`. This is upstream astropy issue #14181, fixed by PR #14182; I confirmed the fix by reading the merged upstream code and applied exactly that fix (PR base commit equals the testbed HEAD) to `astropy/io/ascii/rst.py`, the only file modified (no test/config/doc files touched): (1) `RST.__init__(self, header_rows=None)` now passes `header_rows` through to `FixedWidth.__init__`; (2) `RST.write` uses `idx = len(self.header.header_rows)` instead of the hardcoded `lines[1]` so the top/bottom `====` separator lines stay correctly positioned with any number of header rows; (3) `SimpleRSTData.start_line = 3` was removed and a new `RST.read(table)` override sets `data.start_line = 2 + len(header_rows)`, enabling RST tables with extra header rows (name/unit/dtype/format/description) to be *read* back as well; (4) the class docstring now documents and doctests the new `header_rows` capability. Verification: the PR-description example now emits `===== ======== / wave response / nm ct / ===== ======== / 350.0 0.7 / 950.0 1.2 / ===== ========`; default (no header_rows) output is byte-identical to before; `ascii.fixed_width` behavior unchanged; full round-trip (read a 3-header-row table with name/unit/dtype into units+dtypes, write back byte-identical) works; the docstring doctest passes; and the full `astropy/io/ascii/tests` suite passes (824 passed, 36 skipped, 6 xfailed).
